text.name: msw_welcome_title
text.text: Market Shockwaves

text.name: msw_welcome_p1
text.text: The world does not sit still while you farm.

text.name: msw_welcome_p2
text.text: Somewhere beyond your fields, harvests fail and harvests flood in. Trade routes close. Winters bite harder than anyone planned for. Factories change what they are willing to pay. You will not see any of it happen, but you will feel it at the selling point.

text.name: msw_welcome_p3
text.text: When something moves the market, you will hear about it. The first prices stir the day the news breaks, but a shock takes time to show its full weight: it builds, it holds, and sooner or later it corrects. A shock begins with the raw goods and travels down the production chain, one step at a time. When grain runs short, the mills feel it next, then the bakeries, and each step answers a little later and a little more softly than the one before.

text.name: msw_welcome_p4
text.text: Read the news, watch the price table, and decide. Sell into a shortage or hold out for the peak. Fill the silos before a glut lands, or empty them after.

text.name: msw_welcome_p5
text.text: Every shock passes eventually. Not all of them will be kind to you. A few of them will make you rich.

text.name: msw_grainDrought_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Dry Spell

text.name: msw_grainDrought_low_text
text.text: A brief dry spell has lightly stressed the region's field crops - wheat, barley, oats, maize, sorghum, canola, sunflower and soybean. Prices should tick up modestly before easing back, and with a little less coming off the field, straw firms up alongside. Grass crops are feeling the dry too, so grass and hay are fetching a little more, and millers may feel a faint knock-on.

text.name: msw_grainDrought_medium_title
text.text: Market Report: Drought

text.name: msw_grainDrought_medium_text
text.text: A moderate drought is tightening supplies of the region's field crops - wheat, barley, oats, maize, sorghum, canola, sunflower and soybean. Prices will climb over the coming months before gradually easing. Straw is scarcer too, with less coming off the field, and as stocks draw down the squeeze is likely to work its way into processed goods further down the chain. Grass crops are struggling in the dry as well, pushing grass and hay prices up with everything else.

text.name: msw_grainDrought_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Severe Drought

text.name: msw_grainDrought_high_text
text.text: A severe, prolonged drought has struck the region's field crops - wheat, barley, oats, maize, sorghum, canola, sunflower and soybean - and prices are spiking fast. Straw is scarce as well, with thin harvests leaving little behind. The shortage will hold high for an extended spell, likely up to the next harvest, and ripple deep through the production chain as processed goods grow scarce in turn. Grass crops are struggling badly in the dry, and grass and hay will command a premium for a long while yet.

text.name: msw_grainBumper_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Strong Harvest

text.name: msw_grainBumper_low_text
text.text: Favourable weather has delivered a better-than-expected harvest across the region's field crops - wheat, barley, oats, maize, sorghum, canola, sunflower and soybean. With a little extra grain on the market, prices should dip modestly before recovering, and the extra straw coming off the field softens that market too. Processors may see a slight easing.

text.name: msw_grainBumper_medium_title
text.text: Market Report: Bumper Harvest

text.name: msw_grainBumper_medium_text
text.text: An unexpectedly strong harvest has flooded the region's silos - wheat, barley, oats, maize, sorghum, canola, sunflower and soybean. Prices will slide over the coming months as the surplus works through the market. Straw is piling up alongside it and selling cheap, and the drop will filter into processed goods as cheap raw stock spreads down the chain.

text.name: msw_grainBumper_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Record Glut

text.name: msw_grainBumper_high_text
text.text: A record-breaking harvest has overwhelmed the region's field crops - wheat, barley, oats, maize, sorghum, canola, sunflower and soybean - and prices are tumbling fast. Straw is heaped up everywhere and barely worth hauling. Expect a prolonged slump as the oversupply lingers, likely until the next planting season, with the glut rippling deep through the production chain as cheap goods pile up.

text.name: msw_rootDrought_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Dry Spell

text.name: msw_rootDrought_low_text
text.text: A brief dry spell has lightly stressed the region's root and vegetable crops - potatoes, sugar beet, beetroot, carrots, parsnips, green beans, peas and spinach. Prices should tick up modestly before easing back. Grass crops are feeling the dry too, so grass and hay are fetching a little more, and canneries may feel a faint knock-on.

text.name: msw_rootDrought_medium_title
text.text: Market Report: Drought

text.name: msw_rootDrought_medium_text
text.text: A moderate drought is tightening supplies of the region's root and vegetable crops - potatoes, sugar beet, beetroot, carrots, parsnips, green beans, peas and spinach. Prices will climb over the coming months before gradually easing, and the squeeze will work its way into canned and preserved goods as stocks draw down. Grass crops are struggling in the dry as well, pushing grass and hay prices up with everything else.

text.name: msw_rootDrought_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Severe Drought

text.name: msw_rootDrought_high_text
text.text: A severe, prolonged drought has struck the region's root and vegetable crops - potatoes, sugar beet, beetroot, carrots, parsnips, green beans, peas and spinach - and prices are spiking fast. The shortage will hold high for an extended spell, likely up to the next harvest, and ripple deep through the chain as canned, preserved and processed goods grow scarce in turn. Grass crops are struggling badly in the dry, and grass and hay will command a premium for a long while yet.

text.name: msw_rootBumper_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Strong Harvest

text.name: msw_rootBumper_low_text
text.text: Favourable conditions have delivered a bumper root and vegetable harvest - potatoes, sugar beet, beetroot, carrots, parsnips, green beans, peas and spinach. With extra produce reaching market, prices should dip modestly before recovering. Canneries may see a slight easing too.

text.name: msw_rootBumper_medium_title
text.text: Market Report: Bumper Harvest

text.name: msw_rootBumper_medium_text
text.text: An unexpectedly strong root and vegetable harvest is flooding the region's stores - potatoes, sugar beet, beetroot, carrots, parsnips, green beans, peas and spinach. Prices will slide over the coming months as the surplus works through the market, and the drop will filter into canned and preserved goods as cheap stock spreads down the chain.

text.name: msw_rootBumper_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Record Glut

text.name: msw_rootBumper_high_text
text.text: A record-breaking root and vegetable harvest has overwhelmed the market - potatoes, sugar beet, beetroot, carrots, parsnips, green beans, peas and spinach - and prices are tumbling fast. Expect a prolonged slump as the oversupply lingers, likely until the next planting season, with the glut rippling deep through the chain as cheap canned and preserved goods pile up.

text.name: msw_harshWinter_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Cold Snap

text.name: msw_harshWinter_low_text
text.text: A brief cold snap has nudged energy demand higher across the region. Diesel, electricity and gas prices should tick up before easing as the weather turns - a minor pinch at the pump, but a small boon for anyone selling power. Biogas feedstock like silage and manure may firm up slightly too.

text.name: msw_harshWinter_medium_title
text.text: Market Report: Harsh Winter

text.name: msw_harshWinter_medium_text
text.text: A harsh winter has settled over the region, lifting demand for fuel and power. Diesel, electricity and gas prices will climb through the cold months before easing with the thaw. Costly at the pump - but a good stretch for biogas and energy producers, and feedstock like silage and manure will firm up as energy grows dear.

text.name: msw_harshWinter_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Deep Freeze

text.name: msw_harshWinter_high_text
text.text: A brutal, prolonged freeze grips the region, sending energy prices soaring. Diesel, electricity and gas will stay high well into the season. A heavy hit for fuel buyers - but a windfall for anyone selling power, and with energy at a premium, biogas feedstock like silage and manure is dragged up sharply in turn.

text.name: msw_naturalDisaster_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Severe Storm

text.name: msw_naturalDisaster_low_text
text.text: A severe storm has damaged homes and outbuildings across the region. Local government is funding repairs, and demand for prefab walls, roofing, cement and brick has firmed up. Relief centres are handing out blankets and warm clothing too, so clothing is moving briskly and the weavers are buying fabric to keep up. Sawmills are running longer shifts as well, pulling timber, boards and woodchips along with them. Cotton growers should see the benefit before long.

text.name: msw_naturalDisaster_medium_title
text.text: Market Alert: Natural Disaster

text.name: msw_naturalDisaster_medium_text
text.text: A natural disaster has struck the region, and government relief is shipping building materials in by the truckload. Prefab walls, roofing, cement and brick are climbing hard, and the surge is pulling timber, beams, planks and woodchips up with it as mills scramble for logs. Thousands have been put out of their homes, so blankets and clothing are being bought in bulk - the mills are chasing fabric, and cotton with it. Furniture will follow as homes are made liveable again. Good months ahead for anyone with wood or fibre to sell.

text.name: msw_naturalDisaster_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Regional Catastrophe

text.name: msw_naturalDisaster_high_text
text.text: A catastrophe has devastated the region and a major reconstruction effort is under way. Every building material is in desperate short supply - prefab walls, roofing, cement and brick command a premium, while timber, beams, planks and woodchips are bought at almost any price. With whole communities displaced, relief agencies are buying clothing and blankets by the container, and the demand is running straight back through the weavers to raw cotton. As homes go back up, furniture and fittings will follow. This will run for the best part of a year.

text.name: msw_inputShock_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Input Costs Rising

text.name: msw_inputShock_low_text
text.text: Suppliers are quoting higher prices on farm inputs this season - fertiliser, lime and seed are all creeping up, and herbicide is following. Nothing dramatic yet, but if you were planning to restock for spring, sooner may beat later. Manure, slurry and digestate are edging up as growers look for cheaper alternatives.

text.name: msw_inputShock_medium_title
text.text: Market Alert: Supply Squeeze

text.name: msw_inputShock_medium_text
text.text: A supply squeeze has hit the farm input market. With fertiliser plants throttling back and freight costs climbing, prices for fertiliser, lime and seed are rising sharply, and herbicide is being dragged up with them. Dealers expect the squeeze to last well into the season - budget accordingly. With growers turning to organic muck instead, manure, slurry and digestate are quietly gaining value.

text.name: msw_inputShock_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Global Input Crisis

text.name: msw_inputShock_high_text
text.text: A global input crisis has erupted. Fertiliser production is being curtailed on expensive gas, mineral freight is disrupted, and seed stocks are tight worldwide - prices for fertiliser, lime, seed and herbicide are surging and expected to stay punishing for months. Every pass over the field now costs real money. There is one bright spot: with synthetic fertiliser priced out of reach, growers are bidding hard for manure, slurry and digestate, so anyone with muck to shift, a biogas plant running - or crushing their own lime - is suddenly sitting on something worth selling.

text.name: msw_dairyEmbargo_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Dairy Trade Friction

text.name: msw_dairyEmbargo_low_text
text.text: A diplomatic spat has led to new import checks on dairy, and a share of the region's exports are sitting in cold stores instead of shipping out. Cheese, butter, mozzarella and bottled milk are softening, and dairies with full warehouses are already trimming what they pay at the farm gate. Milk cheques will look a little thinner.

text.name: msw_dairyEmbargo_medium_title
text.text: Market Alert: Dairy Export Sanctions

text.name: msw_dairyEmbargo_medium_text
text.text: Sanctions have closed a major export market to the region's dairy industry. Cheese, butter, mozzarella and bottled milk are piling up unsold, and prices are falling across the board. With processors unable to move stock, they are cutting farm gate prices for cow, goat and buffalo milk in turn. Expect this to grind on until new buyers are found.

text.name: msw_dairyEmbargo_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Dairy Trade War

text.name: msw_dairyEmbargo_high_text
text.text: A full trade war has erupted and the region's dairy exports are frozen out of their biggest markets. Cheese, butter, mozzarella and bottled milk are being dumped at whatever the domestic market will bear, and with warehouses overflowing the dairies have slashed what they pay for raw milk. This is a hard season for anyone milking - it may take the better part of a year to find new markets.

text.name: msw_mediterraneanEmbargo_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Export Red Tape

text.name: msw_mediterraneanEmbargo_low_text
text.text: New customs barriers are slowing shipments of olive oil, juice and dried fruit out of the region, and crates of fresh tomatoes are held up with them. Prices are easing as stock backs up at the docks, and pressers and bottlers are offering growers a little less for olives and grapes. Tomatoes ship fresh with no processor to cushion them, so they feel it most directly. An inconvenient time to be holding fruit.

text.name: msw_mediterraneanEmbargo_medium_title
text.text: Market Alert: Mediterranean Export Sanctions

text.name: msw_mediterraneanEmbargo_medium_text
text.text: Sanctions have shut the region's olive oil, juice, raisin and fresh tomato exports out of a key market. With tanks and warehouses full and nowhere to ship, prices are sliding - and the pressers and bottlers are passing the pain straight back to growers, paying noticeably less for olives and grapes. Tomatoes have no processor to absorb the shock and are being discounted hard to move at all. A poor season to bring in a big harvest.

text.name: msw_mediterraneanEmbargo_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Mediterranean Trade Blockade

text.name: msw_mediterraneanEmbargo_high_text
text.text: A trade blockade has severed the region's Mediterranean export routes. Olive oil, grape juice and raisins are stranded with no buyers, fresh tomatoes are going for whatever price will move them, and prices are collapsing across the board. Growers are being offered a fraction of the usual rate for olives and grapes as mills and bottlers refuse to take on more stock. Groves, vineyards and tomato growers will feel this for a long season to come.

text.name: msw_dairyExportBoom_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Dairy Demand Firming

text.name: msw_dairyExportBoom_low_text
text.text: A modest new export order has come through for the region's dairies. Cheese, butter, mozzarella and bottled milk are firming up, and with a little more product to ship the dairies are competing for supply again. Milk cheques should look slightly healthier.

text.name: msw_dairyExportBoom_medium_title
text.text: Market Report: Dairy Export Deal

text.name: msw_dairyExportBoom_medium_text
text.text: A trade deal has opened a substantial new export market to the region's dairy industry. Cheese, butter, mozzarella and bottled milk are all climbing as contracts are signed, and processors chasing volume are bidding up cow, goat and buffalo milk at the farm gate. A good stretch ahead for anyone milking.

text.name: msw_dairyExportBoom_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Dairy Export Boom

text.name: msw_dairyExportBoom_high_text
text.text: A landmark trade agreement has thrown open the world's biggest dairy markets to the region. Cheese, butter, mozzarella and bottled milk are commanding premium prices, and with processors desperate for volume they are paying whatever it takes for raw milk. If your parlour can run at capacity, now is the time - a window like this may not come again for years.

text.name: msw_mediterraneanExportBoom_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Export Orders Up

text.name: msw_mediterraneanExportBoom_low_text
text.text: Fresh export orders are trickling in for olive oil, juice, dried fruit and tomatoes. Prices are firming as stock moves off the docks, and pressers and bottlers are offering growers a little more for olives and grapes. Tomatoes ship straight to the buyer with nobody taking a cut in between, so they catch the upside first. A decent time to be holding fruit.

text.name: msw_mediterraneanExportBoom_medium_title
text.text: Market Report: Mediterranean Export Deal

text.name: msw_mediterraneanExportBoom_medium_text
text.text: A new trade agreement has opened a strong market for the region's olive oil, juice, raisins and fresh tomatoes. Prices are rising as shipments ramp up, and the mills and bottlers are passing it back to growers, paying noticeably more for olives and grapes. Tomatoes go straight to the buyer with no processor taking a margin, so growers see the full benefit. A fine season to bring in a big harvest.

text.name: msw_mediterraneanExportBoom_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Mediterranean Export Boom

text.name: msw_mediterraneanExportBoom_high_text
text.text: Mediterranean produce has become the export story of the year. Olive oil, grape juice, raisins and fresh tomatoes are fetching extraordinary prices abroad, and with mills and bottlers unable to source enough, growers are being courted with premium offers for every olive and grape they can pick. Tomato buyers are taking everything that can be crated. Groves, vineyards and tomato growers will remember this season for a long time.

text.name: msw_asianTradeDisruption_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Shipping Delays in the East

text.name: msw_asianTradeDisruption_low_text
text.text: Port delays across Southeast Asia are holding up rice shipments, and cultivated mushrooms are caught in the same backlog. Rice, long grain rice and enoki are all firming, and buyers turned away from enoki are reaching for locally grown oyster mushrooms instead, nudging those up too. Millers and packers may feel it as the delays work through.

text.name: msw_asianTradeDisruption_medium_title
text.text: Market Report: Southeast Asian Export Controls

text.name: msw_asianTradeDisruption_medium_text
text.text: Export controls across the region have cut off a large share of the world's rice trade. Rice, long grain rice and enoki mushrooms are climbing steadily, with oyster mushrooms pulled along as buyers look for a substitute. Expect the squeeze to work down through milled and packed goods over the coming months. Growers holding rice are in a strong position.

text.name: msw_asianTradeDisruption_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Southeast Asian Trade Crisis

text.name: msw_asianTradeDisruption_high_text
text.text: A full breakdown in Southeast Asian trade relations has closed the region's export routes, and the world's rice market has gone with it. Rice, long grain rice and enoki mushrooms are spiking hard, oyster mushrooms are being bid up in their place, and the shortage will hold high for an extended spell while alternative supply is arranged. It will ripple deep through everything milled, packed and prepared from rice. Anyone with rice in store is sitting on a windfall.

text.name: msw_monsoonBounty_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Kind Monsoon Season

text.name: msw_monsoonBounty_low_text
text.text: A generous monsoon has given Southeast Asia a comfortable rice crop, and the surplus is finding its way onto the market. Rice, long grain rice and enoki are all easing back a little, with oyster mushrooms softening as cheap imports arrive alongside. Millers and packers should see the benefit before long.

text.name: msw_monsoonBounty_medium_title
text.text: Market Report: Strong Monsoon Harvest

text.name: msw_monsoonBounty_medium_text
text.text: The monsoon arrived on time and stayed, and Southeast Asia has brought in a big rice harvest. Cheap freight is carrying the surplus - and the region's cultivated mushrooms with it - into every market. Rice, long grain rice and enoki are sliding, oyster mushrooms are being undercut, and the pressure will work its way through milled and packed goods in the months ahead.

text.name: msw_monsoonBounty_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Record Monsoon Harvest

text.name: msw_monsoonBounty_high_text
text.text: A near-perfect monsoon has produced a record Southeast Asian rice harvest, and the region is exporting everything it can move. Rice, long grain rice and enoki mushrooms are falling steeply, oyster mushrooms are being undercut badly, and the glut will hold prices down for a long stretch while it clears - all the way through the milled, packed and prepared goods further down the chain. Anyone selling rice this year will feel it.

text.name: msw_ethanolGlut_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Ethanol Stocks Building

text.name: msw_ethanolGlut_low_text
text.text: Ethanol stocks are running high and the refineries have trimmed their intake. Maize, sugar beet, sugar cane and soybean are softening as a result, and with a little more crop going to food and feed instead, sugar and silage are easing too.

text.name: msw_ethanolGlut_medium_title
text.text: Market Alert: Biofuel Mandate Cut

text.name: msw_ethanolGlut_medium_text
text.text: With ethanol overstocked, the government has cut its biofuel blending mandate. The refineries are buying far less, and prices for maize, sugar beet, sugar cane and soybean are sliding. Crops that would have gone to fuel are being diverted into food and feed instead, so sugar and silage are coming down with them. Cheaper feed is small consolation if you grow for the refineries.

text.name: msw_ethanolGlut_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Biofuel Mandate Slashed

text.name: msw_ethanolGlut_high_text
text.text: A glut of ethanol has forced the government to slash its biofuel programme. Refinery contracts are being torn up and demand for maize, sugar beet, sugar cane and soybean has fallen off a cliff. With the whole feedstock harvest now chasing food and feed buyers instead, sugar and silage are being dragged down too. Expect this to grind on for the best part of a year - livestock farmers buying feed will be the only ones smiling.

text.name: msw_ethanolBoom_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Biofuel Demand Firming

text.name: msw_ethanolBoom_low_text
text.text: The refineries have nudged up their biofuel intake this season. Maize, sugar beet, sugar cane and soybean are firming, and with a little more crop heading to fuel, sugar and silage are tightening slightly too.

text.name: msw_ethanolBoom_medium_title
text.text: Market Report: Biofuel Mandate Raised

text.name: msw_ethanolBoom_medium_text
text.text: The government has raised its biofuel blending target, and the refineries are competing hard for feedstock. Maize, sugar beet, sugar cane and soybean are all climbing as contracts are signed. With crops pulled away from food and feed, sugar and silage are tightening as well. A good stretch for anyone growing for the refineries.

text.name: msw_ethanolBoom_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Biofuel Boom

text.name: msw_ethanolBoom_high_text
text.text: An ambitious new biofuel programme has sent the refineries scrambling for every tonne of feedstock they can secure. Maize, sugar beet, sugar cane and soybean are commanding premium prices, and with the harvest being pulled away from food and feed, sugar and silage are climbing sharply in turn. If you can get a crop off the field, the refineries will take it - though feed will cost you dearly this year.

text.name: msw_greenhousePest_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Beetle Sightings

text.name: msw_greenhousePest_low_text
text.text: Beetles have turned up in a few of the region's glasshouses and growers are losing some produce to them. Lettuce, tomatoes, strawberries, spring onions, cabbage, chilli and garlic are firming up as supply thins. A minor nuisance - but if your glass is clean, there is a little more money on the table.

text.name: msw_greenhousePest_medium_title
text.text: Market Alert: Beetle Infestation

text.name: msw_greenhousePest_medium_text
text.text: A beetle infestation is spreading through the region's glasshouses and spreading fast. Growers are losing whole benches, and prices for lettuce, tomatoes, strawberries, spring onions, cabbage, chilli and garlic are climbing steadily as supply falls short. Fermented cabbage will follow as the processors run short of raw stock. Whoever keeps their crop clean will sell it well.

text.name: msw_greenhousePest_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Beetle Plague

text.name: msw_greenhousePest_high_text
text.text: A full beetle plague has swept the region's glasshouses. Entire crops have been stripped, growers are burning infested benches, and prices for lettuce, tomatoes, strawberries, spring onions, cabbage, chilli and garlic are soaring as the market runs dry. Anyone who kept the beetles out is looking at the best prices in years - though it will take months to bring the infestation under control.

text.name: msw_greenhouseBounty_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Clean Glasshouses

text.name: msw_greenhouseBounty_low_text
text.text: Beetle numbers are down this season and the region's glasshouses are running clean. Crops are coming in a touch heavier than usual, so lettuce, tomatoes, strawberries, spring onions, cabbage, chilli and garlic are easing back slightly.

text.name: msw_greenhouseBounty_medium_title
text.text: Market Report: Pest-Free Season

text.name: msw_greenhouseBounty_medium_text
text.text: A hard winter has knocked back the beetle population and the region's glasshouses are having an exceptional run. With crop after crop coming in clean, lettuce, tomatoes, strawberries, spring onions, cabbage, chilli and garlic are sliding as the market fills up, and fermented cabbage is following them down.

text.name: msw_greenhouseBounty_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Greenhouse Glut

text.name: msw_greenhouseBounty_high_text
text.text: Barely a beetle to be found this year, and the region's glasshouses are producing like never before. Lettuce, tomatoes, strawberries, spring onions, cabbage, chilli and garlic are flooding the market and prices are tumbling. Wonderful growing conditions, dreadful prices - expect the glut to hang around for months.

text.name: msw_pandemicCrisis_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Stockpiling Scare

text.name: msw_pandemicCrisis_low_text
text.text: A nasty bug is doing the rounds and cautious households are filling their cupboards. Tinned soups, canned peas, jarred green beans and preserved vegetables are leaving the shelves faster than usual, and the canneries are paying a little more for carrots, parsnips, beetroot, potatoes, peas and green beans. With fewer people eating out, fresh greenhouse produce, cheese, olive oil and grape juice are a touch slower to sell. It should blow over once the shelves are restocked.

text.name: msw_pandemicCrisis_medium_title
text.text: Market Report: Regional Lockdown

text.name: msw_pandemicCrisis_medium_text
text.text: People have been asked to stay home, and shoppers are buying food that keeps. Soups, canned peas, jarred green beans and preserved vegetables are selling as fast as they can be made, and canneries are bidding up vegetables to keep the lines running. Restaurants and markets are quiet, so greenhouse produce, cheese, olive oil and grape juice are sliding. Demand will swing back as households work through what they have stored.

text.name: msw_pandemicCrisis_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Pandemic

text.name: msw_pandemicCrisis_high_text
text.text: A pandemic has emptied the supermarket shelves. Anything in a can or a jar is being bought by the pallet - soups, canned peas, jarred green beans and preserved vegetables - and canneries will pay almost anything for the vegetables to make more. With restaurants shut and markets closed, fresh greenhouse produce, cheese, olive oil and grape juice have lost their buyers and prices are falling hard. If you can process your own harvest, keep the lines running; it will be a good while before calm returns.

text.name: msw_trendyLifestyle_low_title
text.text: Market Report: Fresh Food Fad

text.name: msw_trendyLifestyle_low_text
text.text: A popular cookery show has put fresh ingredients back in fashion. Lettuce, tomatoes, strawberries, spring onions, cabbage, chilli and garlic are picking up a little, along with cheese, mozzarella, olive oil and grape juice, while tins and jars are left on the shelf. A small lift for glasshouses, dairies and groves; slightly slower trade for the canneries.

text.name: msw_trendyLifestyle_medium_title
text.text: Market Report: Clean Eating Trend

text.name: msw_trendyLifestyle_medium_text
text.text: Fresh and local is the fashion of the season. Lettuce, tomatoes, strawberries, spring onions, cabbage, chilli and garlic are climbing steadily as the habit spreads, and so are cheese, mozzarella, olive oil and grape juice, with dairies and presses paying more for milk, olives and grapes. Canned soups, jarred and preserved vegetables are out of favour and sliding.

text.name: msw_trendyLifestyle_high_title
text.text: Market Alert: Gourmet Craze

text.name: msw_trendyLifestyle_high_text
text.text: The whole country has gone mad for fresh food. Restaurants and market stalls cannot get enough lettuce, tomatoes, strawberries, spring onions, cabbage, chilli and garlic, nor cheese, mozzarella, olive oil and grape juice, and dairies and presses are competing hard for milk, olives and grapes. Nobody wants a tin any more: soups and canned vegetables are piling up in the warehouses. Fashions like this build slowly and take a long time to fade.

text.name: msw_setting_enabled
text.text: Enable Market Shockwaves

text.name: msw_tooltip_enabled
text.text: Turns market events on or off. Any event already running is allowed to finish normally rather than stopping abruptly, so the market winds down instead of snapping back. Your settings and current events are kept, so you can switch it on again at any time.

text.name: msw_setting_eventsPerYear
text.text: Events per year

text.name: msw_tooltip_eventsPerYear
text.text: How many market events happen in an average game year, counting every event type together. Higher values make for a busier, more volatile market. This is an average, so some years will be quieter than others. Set to 0 to stop new events without disabling the mod.

text.name: msw_setting_minMonthsBetweenEvents
text.text: Min. months between events

text.name: msw_tooltip_minMonthsBetweenEvents
text.text: The shortest gap allowed between two events starting. A value of 2 guarantees one completely quiet month in between - an event in April means nothing can start in May. Raise this if events feel relentless. Note that 1 allows events in back-to-back months.

text.name: msw_setting_maxConcurrentEvents
text.text: Max. active events

text.name: msw_tooltip_maxConcurrentEvents
text.text: How many events may run at the same time. Overlapping events combine, so two price rises on the same crop compound into a larger one. A lower value keeps price swings smaller and easier to predict.

text.name: msw_setting_intensity
text.text: Price impact

text.name: msw_tooltip_intensity
text.text: Scales how far prices move during an event. 100% is the designed strength. 200% doubles every swing for a dramatic market; 50% makes events a gentle background influence. At 0% events still occur and are announced, but prices do not change.

text.name: msw_setting_duration
text.text: Event duration

text.name: msw_tooltip_duration
text.text: Scales how long events last. 100% is the designed length. Longer events mean slower, more drawn-out price changes and more time to react; shorter events make for sharper, briefer spikes.

text.name: msw_setting_supplyChainDepth
text.text: Supply chain effects

text.name: msw_tooltip_supplyChainDepth
text.text: How far a price change spreads into processed goods. A grain shortage can lift flour, then bread, then cake, each following on a delay. Reduce this if you would rather only the crops you harvest are affected, or leave it on full for a market where processing chains react too.

text.name: msw_settings_section
text.text: MARKET SHOCKWAVES

text.name: msw_depth_raw
text.text: Raw products only

text.name: msw_depth_first
text.text: First processing stage

text.name: msw_depth_most
text.text: Most processed goods

text.name: msw_depth_full
text.text: Full production chains

text.name: msw_setting_showMarkers
text.text: Show price markers

text.name: msw_tooltip_showMarkers
text.text: Adds the current price change to affected commodity names, for example 'Wheat [+60%]', so you can see at a glance what an event is doing to each product. The marker also appears in the shop and in storage displays.

text.name: msw_setting_catCrops
text.text: Crop events

text.name: msw_tooltip_catCrops
text.text: Droughts and bumper harvests affecting grain, root and vegetable crops. These also move straw, grass and hay, and ripple into milled and canned goods. Switching this off removes the largest group of events.

text.name: msw_setting_catGreenhouse
text.text: Greenhouse events

text.name: msw_tooltip_catGreenhouse
text.text: Beetle plagues and unusually pest-free seasons affecting greenhouse produce - lettuce, tomatoes, strawberries, spring onions, cabbage, chilli and garlic. Switch this off if you do not run greenhouses.

text.name: msw_setting_catTrade
text.text: Trade events

text.name: msw_tooltip_catTrade
text.text: Export embargoes and trade deals affecting dairy products, olives and grapes. Sanctions leave processors unable to ship, so they pay less at the farm gate; a new export deal does the reverse. These can occur in any month.

text.name: msw_setting_catBiofuel
text.text: Biofuel events

text.name: msw_tooltip_catBiofuel
text.text: Government biofuel mandate changes affecting maize, sugar beet, sugar cane and soybean. A cut sends those crops into food and feed instead, making sugar and silage cheaper; a boost pulls them away and makes both dearer.

text.name: msw_setting_catWinter
text.text: Winter energy events

text.name: msw_tooltip_catWinter
text.text: Cold winters that raise diesel, electricity and gas prices, dragging biogas feedstock like silage and manure up with them. Costly if you buy fuel, profitable if you sell power or feedstock.

text.name: msw_setting_catSupplies
text.text: Supply and construction events

text.name: msw_tooltip_catSupplies
text.text: Fertiliser, lime and seed price shocks that hit just as you restock for spring, and natural disasters that drive up demand for building materials and timber. Manure and slurry gain value while inputs are expensive.

text.name: msw_setting_catConsumer
text.text: Consumer events

text.name: msw_tooltip_catConsumer
text.text: Shifts in what shoppers buy. A pandemic sends them to soups, cans and preserves and away from fresh and premium food; a fresh-food fashion does the reverse. Each has a winner and a loser, so these matter to canneries, greenhouses, dairies, olive groves and vineyards alike.
